statement: One printer prints a set of exam papers in 20 minutes. A second printer prints the same set in 30 minutes. How many minutes do the two printers take to print one set together, sharing the work?

choices.misconception: I halved the faster printer's time, as if adding the second printer doubled the speed.
I halved the slower printer's time, as if the two printers worked at the same rate.
I took the average of 20 and 30, which gives the time for one printer of average speed, not for two working together.
I added the two times, as if one printer had to finish before the other could start.

hints: How much of the job does each printer do in one minute?
Combined work: add rates, not times. Turn each time into a fraction of the job per minute, add the fractions, then turn the total rate back into a time.
In one minute the printers do 1/20 and 1/30 of the set. Find a common denominator.

solutions.reliable: In one minute the first printer does 1/20 of the set and the second 1/30. Together that is 3/60 + 2/60 = 5/60 = 1/12 of the set per minute, so the set takes 12 minutes. The transferable idea: rates add, times do not, so convert times to rates before combining.
solutions.elegant: In 60 minutes the first printer prints 3 sets and the second 2 sets, so together 5 sets in 60 minutes, which is one set every 12 minutes.

whyOnTest: Work-rate questions test that rates add while times do not, and every distractor here combines the times directly.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
